result.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
result.summary: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. To assess where it helps, we compare its use as an optimizer, performance predictor, and region guider against conventional methods and a large language model (LLM) on eight AI tuning tasks. Conventional optimizers attain rank 1 in six of eight comparisons. Similarly, established predictors outperform Jev in seven. Through region guidance, however, it finds configurations with lower perplexity than those selected by the native tuner, offering a quality gain when additional decision time and API fees are acceptable. These findings yield actionable recommendations on selecting the decision role, retaining conventional predictors, and balancing tuning quality against cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察通用决策模型（以 Jev 为代表）能否指导 AI 配置调优，在八个调优任务上将其分别作为优化器、性能预测器和区域引导器与传统方法及 LLM 对比，发现仅在区域引导角色下、允许额外决策时间与费用时可获得质量提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「额外决策时间与 API 成本换取质量」的角色分工结论，可能与 LVR 中多花 latent 计算步是否值得、如何决定继续搜索或停止的问题形成类比，可供核查而非已验证的迁移。
